That’s my case. I’m not Jewish, so my children aren’t either. We’ve been living here in Givat Olga for five years.

In our little world, in our own environment, and with the people we have around us, there’s no problem at all. My children are proudly Argentine. They know they’re not considered Jewish, but honestly, they don’t really care, and it’s never been an issue. They like being different and enjoy that difference. We celebrate Christmas, too.

What I did, to be completely honest, was choose places where they would feel comfortable. My children go to a democratic school, where people are very open-minded, kind, and accepting of differences. I don’t think it’s necessarily the same in traditional schools, and even less so in religious schools. I really don’t think it would be the same.

For now, everything is going well. And if they ever face difficulties, I believe they’ll learn how to talk about differences and understand that when someone discriminates, the problem belongs to the person discriminating, not to them.

So, for now, everything is fine. ❤️

If there’s anything I can do to help you, just let me know.
